expeditions.name: 43rd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica
expeditions.title: 43rd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica
expeditions.institution: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Ministry of Earth Sciences
expeditions.summary: The 43rd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica (ISEA) operated out of Bharati Station in the Larsemann Hills and Maitri Station, conducting critical glaciological, geological, and atmospheric research during the 2023-24 season.
keyFindings: Coastal ice edge melted three days earlier than the previous summer average
Tiny sea plants bloomed in higher numbers near fresh meltwater pools
Clean air readings showed almost zero artificial dust or soot

stops.name: Return Passage via Southern Indian Ocean

events.title: Departure from Cape Town
events.description: Crew and scientific equipment board the polar research charter to cross the roaring forties.

events.title: First Ice Shelf Encounter at Prydz Bay
events.description: Vessel reached heavy pack ice and deployed satellite navigation floats to guide the final approach.

events.title: Arrival and Setup at Bharati Station
events.description: Summer research team relieved winter crew, initiating meteorological sensors and melt pool collection.

events.title: Survey at Dålk Glacier Melt Outlet
events.description: Team measured accelerated fresh meltwater streams discharging into the coastal marine bay.

events.title: Homeward Passage through Southern Indian Ocean
events.description: Winterizing station instruments and transporting core ice samples back to Goa for analysis.

expeditions.agency: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), MoES
expeditions.missionMandate: Authorized under the Indian Antarctic Program and governed by the landmark Indian Antarctic Act 2022, this mission executed primary field mandates in cryospheric mass balance, paleoclimate reconstruction, and high-latitude terrestrial ecology across Queen Maud Land and the Larsemann Hills. Scientific contingents worked under zero-waste environmental protocols mandated by the Committee for Environmental Protection (CEP) of the Antarctic Treaty.
expeditions.logisticsOverview: Operations relied on chartered polar-class ice-strengthened vessels (such as MV Vasiliy Golovnin and SA Agulhas), paired with heavy PistenBully 300 Polar tracked groomers and Kamov Ka-32 heavy-lift helicopters for ship-to-shore sling cargo transfers over blue-ice runways. Field camps maintained satellite links via Inmarsat and Indian GSAT constellations, operating in temperatures dropping to -42°C with sustained katabatic blizzards exceeding 150 km/h.
expeditions.climateSignificance: Measurements in East Antarctica serve as direct barometers for the global thermohaline conveyor belt and global sea-level projections. Ice shelves in this sector buttress massive continental ice sheets; monitoring grounding-line stability and sub-ice shelf oceanic heat fluxes directly informs models predicting sea-level changes along India's 7,516-kilometer vulnerable coastline.
participatingInstitutions: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa
India Meteorological Department (IMD), New Delhi
Geological Survey of India (GSI), Polar Division
National Institute of Oceanography (CSIR-NIO), Goa
Indian Institute of Geomagnetism (IIG), Navi Mumbai
Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), Mumbai

expeditions.name: 42nd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica
expeditions.title: 42nd Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica
expeditions.institution: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Ministry of Earth Sciences
expeditions.summary: The 42nd ISEA successfully completed wintering operations at Maitri Station in the Schirmacher Oasis, maintaining continuous meteorological observations, lake ecological monitoring, and atmospheric physics experiments.
keyFindings: Lake Priyadarshini water remained clear and stable under thick winter ice
Winter winds reached top speeds of 165 kilometers per hour without station damage
Team sleep patterns stabilized after introducing scheduled warm-light lamps

events.title: Convoy Departure from Cape Town
events.description: Polar ship set sail laden with year-round fuel, food containers, and laboratory modules.

events.title: Ice Shelf Landing at Princess Astrid Coast
events.description: Cargos were transferred to heavy tracked PistenBully sledges for the inland ice crossing.

events.title: Taking Command of Maitri Base
events.description: Winter-over team officially assumed control of life support systems, boilers, and scientific towers.

events.title: Deep Winter Sampling at Lake Priyadarshini
events.description: Cores extracted through two meters of lake ice revealed stable, pristine freshwater ecosystems.

events.title: Spring Mast Maintenance & Handover
events.description: Calibrated wind turbines and high-latitude sky cameras in preparation for incoming relief convoy.

expeditions.name: 44th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica
expeditions.title: 44th Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica
expeditions.institution: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Ministry of Earth Sciences
expeditions.summary: The 44th ISEA initiated deep inland logistical traverses, establishing automated weather telemetry links and preparing initial site surveys for the upcoming green research base Maitri II.
keyFindings: Five new automated weather towers began sending hourly wind and temperature updates
Overland convoy completed the 300-kilometer ice crossing safely in nine days
Early snow tests show fresh winter buildup along the coastal ice shelf

events.title: Docking at Bharati Coastal Base
events.description: Unloaded modern autonomous solar-wind weather towers and specialized ice coring drills.

events.title: Overland Ice Crossing Midpoint
events.description: Tracked convoy safely traversed blue-ice crevasses between Bharati and Maitri.

events.title: Arrival at Maitri Station
events.description: Installed high-frequency satellite telemetry links transmitting live data directly to India.

events.title: Field Research in Central Dronning Maud Land
events.description: Currently testing automated snow radar sensors along the polar plateau.

expeditions.name: Indian Arctic Winter Expedition 2024
expeditions.title: Indian Arctic Winter Expedition 2024
expeditions.institution: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Ministry of Earth Sciences
expeditions.summary: India's landmark 2023-24 winter Arctic expedition at Himadri Station, Ny-Ålesund (78°55'N), maintaining year-round atmospheric, cryospheric, and marine observatory operations.
keyFindings: Fjord waters stayed ice-free for two weeks longer than a decade ago
Night sky cameras captured 47 active aurora displays during dark months
Tiny airborne sea salt particles were detected further inland than expected

events.title: Staging in Longyearbyen
events.description: Safety orientation, arctic rifle training, and cold-weather equipment checks in Svalbard's capital.

events.title: Arrival at Himadri Base
events.description: Settled into India's northernmost station as polar darkness descended over the valley.

events.title: Midwinter Mooring Check in Kongsfjorden
events.description: Recovered underwater sensor logs recording Atlantic ocean brine warmth.

events.title: Atmospheric Aerosol Sampling at Zeppelin
events.description: Measured trace greenhouse gases and northern light geomagnetic perturbations.

events.title: Winter Expedition Conclusion
events.description: Handed station over to summer researchers as the sun re-emerged over the Arctic peaks.

expeditions.agency: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), MoES
expeditions.missionMandate: Conducted under India's Arctic Policy ('India and the Arctic: building a partnership for sustainable development') from Himadri Station in Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard (78°55'N). The expedition focused on Arctic amplification, glacial runoff hydrochemistry, atmospheric aerosol optical depth, and marine microbial adaptations in Kongsfjorden, adhering strictly to Svalbard Environmental Protection regulations.
expeditions.logisticsOverview: Scientists operated out of the Kings Bay international scientific research village in Ny-Ålesund, accessing glacial snouts and outer fjord waters using specialized marine research tenders (MS Teisten) and snowmobiles. Field safety included mandatory polar bear safety protocols, high-frequency radio beacons, and immersion survival suits during open-water fjord sampling.
expeditions.climateSignificance: The rapid melting of Arctic sea ice directly modulates the mid-latitude jet stream, triggering planetary wave oscillations that perturb the Indian Summer Monsoon Rainfall (ISMR). Investigating Arctic teleconnections is vital for improving seasonal monsoon forecasts relied upon by hundreds of millions of Indian farmers.
participatingInstitutions: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa
National Institute of Technology (NIT) / MoES Cryosphere Unit
Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru
Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CSIR-CCMB), Hyderabad
National Remote Sensing Centre (ISRO-NRSC), Hyderabad

expeditions.name: Indian Arctic Summer Campaign 2025
expeditions.title: Indian Arctic Summer Campaign 2025
expeditions.institution: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Ministry of Earth Sciences
expeditions.summary: The 2025 Indian Arctic Summer Campaign focused on glacial runoff dynamics, fjord oceanography in Kongsfjorden, and IndARC moored observatory data retrieval.
keyFindings: Glacier melt stream runoff volume increased by 8 percent during peak midday sun
Seabirds gathered in larger flocks near fresh runoff outlets to feed on stunned krill
Underwater listening sensors logged daily glacier calving sounds across the bay

events.title: Field Team Arrives in Svalbard
events.description: Marine ecologists and hydrologists landed with acoustic hydrophones and water testing kits.

events.title: Himadri Lab Calibration
events.description: Calibrated spectrophotometers and acoustic recorders to track glacier melting noise.

events.title: Kronebreen Glacier Field Runoff Study
events.description: Observed rapid freshwater release into the seawater and documented seabird feeding swarms.

events.title: Ocean Brine Salinity Profiling
events.description: Lowered CTD instruments into outer fjord channels to track meltwater layering.

events.title: Coastal Micro-organism Collection
events.description: Ongoing biodiversity tracking along the gravel beaches of Blomstrand peninsula.

expeditions.name: Indian Arctic Summer Expedition 2023
expeditions.title: Indian Arctic Summer Expedition 2023
expeditions.institution: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Ministry of Earth Sciences
expeditions.summary: The 2023 Summer Arctic campaign centered on permafrost active-layer dynamics, tundra soil microbiology, and collaborative experiments at the Ny-Ålesund International Research Facility.
keyFindings: Tundra moss patches expanded outward by nearly two centimeters in sunny hollows
Microscopic soil fungi survived brief freezing spells during early summer nights
Snowmelt ponds dried up four days quicker than records from five years ago

events.title: Summer Campaign Inauguration
events.description: Botanists and permafrost researchers opened the seasonal soil laboratory at Himadri.

events.title: Moraine Plant Succession Census
events.description: Mapped slow-growing Arctic willow and saxifrage blooms in newly deglaciated valleys.

events.title: Soil Core Drilling at Stuphallet
events.description: Extracted permafrost soil samples to culture cold-tolerant protective enzymes in bacteria.

events.title: Bayelva Melt Discharge Census
events.description: Monitored sediment discharge carried by summer snowmelt into the coastal fjord.

events.title: Sample Preservation and Return
events.description: Packed 200 soil jars in thermal dry containers for flight dispatch to Goa.

expeditions.name: 12th Indian Southern Ocean Expedition
expeditions.title: 12th Indian Southern Ocean Expedition
expeditions.institution: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Ministry of Earth Sciences
expeditions.summary: The 12th Southern Ocean Expedition carried out multidisciplinary transects across the Subtropical, Subantarctic, and Polar Fronts to quantify the ocean's role as a global carbon sink.
keyFindings: Stormy winds drove cold surface water down to 400 meters depth
The Polar Front zone acted as a strong sponge for atmospheric carbon
Large pods of humpback whales were spotted feeding along ice edges

events.title: Departure from Mauritius
events.description: Research vessel ORV Sagar Kanya sailed into open seas with oceanographers and geochemists.

events.title: Sub-Tropical Front Ocean Casts
events.description: Lowered rosette water samplers to 2,000 meters to measure carbon content shifts.

events.title: Entering the Roaring Polar Front
events.description: Recorded gale winds churning sea bubbles, demonstrating massive natural carbon absorption.

events.title: Ice Edge Marine Mammal Survey
events.description: Spotted pods of humpback whales and recorded sub-zero ocean surface temperature drops.

events.title: Cruise Completion at Port Louis
events.description: Successfully landed 480 deep-sea water bottles for laboratory testing in India.

expeditions.missionMandate: Dispatched into the volatile Roaring Forties, Furious Fifties, and Shrieking Sixties aboard oceanographic research vessels (ORV Sagar Nidhi and chartered icebreakers). Mandated by MoES to sample the Subtropical Front, Subantarctic Front, and Polar Front to quantify oceanic carbon sequestration and heat uptake in the Southern Ocean.
expeditions.logisticsOverview: The voyage covered over 8,500 nautical miles across extreme Southern Ocean swells exceeding 12 meters. Scientific teams deployed 24-bottle CTD rosette carousels, 150 kHz Acoustic Doppler Current Profilers (ADCP), Autonomous Underwater Floats (Argo), and multi-net zooplankton trawls across depths down to 4,500 meters under severe gale conditions.
expeditions.climateSignificance: The Southern Ocean accounts for more than 40% of all anthropogenic carbon dioxide absorbed by the global oceans and over 75% of excess oceanic heat uptake. Understanding iron limitation and biological carbon pump efficiency here is key to projecting global atmospheric CO2 trajectories.
participatingInstitutions: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa
National Institute of Oceanography (CSIR-NIO), Goa
Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), Hyderabad
School of Earth, Ocean and Climate Sciences, IIT Bhubaneswar

expeditions.name: 13th Indian Southern Ocean Expedition
expeditions.title: 13th Indian Southern Ocean Expedition
expeditions.institution: National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Ministry of Earth Sciences
expeditions.summary: Conducted onboard MoES research vessel ORV Sagar Nidhi, deploying autonomous profiling floats, glider systems, and bio-optical sensors to trace Circumpolar Deep Water upwelling.
keyFindings: Deployed eight long-lasting robotic floats across sub-Antarctic waters
Detected a cool subsurface water layer moving eastward toward Australia
Recorded ocean sound levels during heavy winter gale force winds

events.title: Cruise Embarkation
events.description: Vessel departed loaded with eight specialized deep-profiling autonomous floats.

events.title: Acoustic Surveys over Kerguelen Plateau
events.description: Charted deep submarine ridges and current speeds connecting Indian and Antarctic waters.

events.title: Autonomous Float Deployment
events.description: Released four battery-powered Argo floats scheduled to beam daily ocean profiles via satellite.

events.title: Continental Shelf Deep Soundings
events.description: Collected core salinity data showing cool Antarctic bottom water flowing eastward.

events.title: Arrival at Mormugao Port, Goa
events.description: Voyage concluded successfully with all floats transmitting active data to the Indian data hub.
